ADHD is one of the most misunderstood neurodevelopmental conditions. Unfortunately, myths and misconceptions can delay diagnosis, increase stigma, and prevent individuals from getting the support they need.

❌ Myth: ADHD is caused by poor parenting.
✅ Fact: ADHD is a neurodevelopmental condition with strong genetic and biological influences.

❌ Myth: Only hyperactive children have ADHD.
✅ Fact: Many individuals, especially girls, may primarily struggle with inattention and organization.

❌ Myth: Children outgrow ADHD.
✅ Fact: While symptoms may change over time, ADHD often continues into adolescence and adulthood.

❌ Myth: ADHD means low intelligence.
✅ Fact: People with ADHD can be highly intelligent, creative, innovative, and successful.

🚨 Common Signs of ADHD in Children 🚨

ADHD is more than just being energetic or easily distracted. It is a neurodevelopmental condition that can affect attention, behavior, emotional regulation, and daily functioning.

✔️ Difficulty paying attention

✔️ Trouble following instructions

Every child may show some of these behaviors occasionally. However, when these difficulties are persistent, occur across different settings (home and school), and interfere with daily life, a professional evaluation may be helpful.

ADHD (Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder) is a neurodevelopmental condition that affects attention, impulse control, and activity levels. It can impact academic performance, work, relationships, and daily functioning, but with proper understanding and support, individuals with ADHD can thrive.

🔹 Inattentive Type

🚩 Early Signs of Autism: What Parents Should Know

Recognizing early developmental differences can help children access support and interventions sooner.

Common early signs may include:
✓ Limited eye contact
✓ Delayed speech or language development
✓ Not responding consistently to their name
✓ Repetitive movements or behaviors
✓ Difficulty engaging in social interactions

Square Breathing (Box Breathing): A Simple Technique for Panic Attacks

When anxiety or panic starts to rise, square breathing can help slow your breathing and calm your body’s stress response.

⬜ Step 1: Breathe in through your nose for 4 seconds
⬜ Step 2: Hold your breath for 4 seconds
⬜ Step 3: Breathe out slowly through your mouth for 4 seconds
⬜ Step 4: Hold your breath again for 4 seconds

Repeat this cycle for 1–3 minutes or until you feel calmer.

Why it helps:
During a panic attack, breathing often becomes rapid and shallow. Square breathing encourages slow, controlled breaths, which can reduce physical symptoms such as a racing heart, dizziness, and feelings of panic.

Remember: Panic attacks are uncomfortable but not dangerous. Controlled breathing can help your body regain a sense of balance and control.

featured_reviews.review_text:
My journey with chronic pain began around 2012–13, following persistent back issues and multiple falls. Over time, the condition gradually worsened, and in 2023, after another fall, I was diagnosed with osteoporosis. Pain in my knee, hip, and back became increasingly severe, eventually affecting even the simplest daily activities.

By August 2024, mobility had reduced significantly, and I was almost bedridden. While surgery was advised, it became clear that rebuilding strength was essential for a successful recovery. At this stage, I began aqua therapy at Aqua Center at Prabhadevi.

The initial phase was challenging, with even basic movements causing discomfort due to widespread muscle tightness and trigger points. However, with consistent guidance and a structured program combining aqua therapy, land-based rehabilitation, and targeted pain-relief techniques, gradual but meaningful improvement was achieved.

In December, I underwent a hip replacement surgery. Following recovery, rehabilitation was resumed with regularity and focus. The clinical expertise, personalised attention, and continuity of care at Aqua Center at Prabhadevi played a vital role in regaining mobility and confidence.

Today, there is a marked improvement in strength, balance, and overall movement. Walking is comfortable again, and there is a renewed sense of control over the body. Beyond physical recovery, the process has helped correct long-standing movement patterns and restore functional independence.

Aqua therapy, along with guided physiotherapy, has been an integral part of this recovery journey. It is highly recommended for individuals managing chronic pain or preparing for and recovering from surgery, as it offers a safe, effective, and truly transformative path to rehabilitation.

A special note of gratitude to Sanya, Pravalika, and Vaibhavi for their dedication, care, and unwavering support throughout this journey. Their expertise and encouragement have made a meaningful difference at every stage of recovery.

ADHD is more than just being energetic or easily distracted. It is a neurodevelopmental condition that can affect attention, behavior, emotional regulation, and daily functioning.

Square Breathing (Box Breathing): A Simple Technique for Panic Attacks

When anxiety or panic starts to rise, square breathing can help slow your breathing and calm your body’s stress response.

⬜ Step 1: Breathe in through your nose for 4 seconds
⬜ Step 2: Hold your breath for 4 seconds
⬜ Step 3: Breathe out slowly through your mouth for 4 seconds
⬜ Step 4: Hold your breath again for 4 seconds

Repeat this cycle for 1–3 minutes or until you feel calmer.

Why it helps:
During a panic attack, breathing often becomes rapid and shallow. Square breathing encourages slow, controlled breaths, which can reduce physical symptoms such as a racing heart, dizziness, and feelings of panic.

Remember: Panic attacks are uncomfortable but not dangerous. Controlled breathing can help your body regain a sense of balance and control.

❄️🔥 Ice vs Heat Therapy – Which One Should You Use?

Many patients with back pain, neck pain, knee pain, sports injuries, and muscle strains often ask whether ice or heat therapy is better.

✅ Ice Therapy is generally recommended for:
• Recent injuries
• Swelling and inflammation
• Sprains and strains
• Acute pain

✅ Heat Therapy is generally recommended for:
• Muscle stiffness
• Chronic pain
• Joint stiffness
• Improving blood circulation

Are you waking up with back pain, stiffness, or discomfort every morning?

Your sleeping position can have a major impact on spinal alignment, muscle relaxation, and pain levels. Choosing the right sleeping posture may help reduce lower back pain, neck pain, and pressure on the spine.

• Sleeping on your side with a pillow between your knees
• Sleeping on your back with a pillow under your knees
• Using a supportive mattress and proper pillow

❌ Avoid:
